title: Proton pump inhibitors in long-term use: increased risk of fracture
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 5, issue 9, April 2012: A2 (republished on GOV.UK 11 December 2014)
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: Observational studies suggest a modest increase in the risk of hip, wrist or spine fracture, especially with high doses and use longer than 1 year, observed mainly in elderly patients; other risk factors may contribute. Two meta-analyses of pharmacoepidemiological studies suggest a 10% to 40% increase above baseline; the primary studies varied in adjustment for other fracture risk factors and for calcium or vitamin D use. Patients at risk of osteoporosis should be treated according to guidelines with adequate vitamin D and calcium. Over-the-counter PPIs should not be used for more than 4 weeks without consulting a doctor.
